title: Human Capital Accumulation across Space
On the Geographic Implications of Carbon Taxes
abstract: A unilateral carbon tax trades off the distortionary costs of taxation and the future gains from slowing down global warming. Because the cost is local and immediate, whereas the benefit is global and delayed, this tradeoff tends to be unfavorable to unilateral carbon taxes. We show that this logic breaks down in a world with trade and migration where economic geography is shaped by agglomeration economies and congestion forces. Using a multisector dynamic spatial integrated assessment model (S-IAM), this paper predicts that a carbon tax introduced by the European Union (EU) and rebated locally can, if not too large, increase the size of Europe’s economy by concentrating economic activity in its high-productivity non-agricultural core and by incentivizing immigration to the EU. The resulting change in the spatial distribution of economic activity improves global efficiency and welfare. A unilateral carbon tax with local rebating introduced by the US generates similar global welfare gains. Other forms of rebating can dilute or revert this positive effect.
abstract_zh: 单边碳税需要在征税的扭曲性成本与减缓全球变暖所带来的未来收益之间进行权衡。由于成本是局部且即时的，而收益是全球性且滞后的，这种权衡往往对单边碳税不利。我们表明，在一个存在贸易与移民、且经济地理由集聚经济和拥挤效应塑造的世界中，这一逻辑并不成立。本文利用一个多部门动态空间综合评估模型（S-IAM）预测，若欧盟（EU）引入碳税并将税收返还给当地，只要税率不过高，便能通过使经济活动集中于其高生产率的非农业核心地区，并激励移民流入欧盟，从而扩大欧洲的经济规模。由此产生的经济活动空间分布变化将提高全球效率并改善福利。美国若实行附带地方返还的单边碳税，也能产生类似的全球福利收益。其他形式的返还方式可能会削弱甚至逆转这一正面效应。

title: Ethnic Remoteness Reduces the Peace Dividend from Trade Access
Evaluating the Spatial Consequences of a Climate Tipping Point
abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a system of ocean currents that plays a key role in regulating global climate, including moderating temperatures in Europe and the North Atlantic. Its potential collapse due to global warming is widely considered one of the more likely climate tipping points. This paper examines the economic implications of such a collapse using a dynamic spatially integrated assessment model (S-IAM) of the world economy. Scandinavia and parts of Russia are predicted to experience significant losses in GDP and welfare, while southern Europe, northern Africa, and Brazil benefit from slightly colder temperatures. S-IAMs generally predict that global warming is especially harmful to low-income regions, but an AMOC collapse could mitigate some of these negative impacts in parts of the developing world while instead harming some of the more advanced economies. This lowers spatial inequality, but global welfare drops by 1.9% by 2200 under an intermediate-emissions scenario. Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.
abstract_zh: 大西洋经向翻转环流（AMOC）是一套洋流系统，在调节全球气候方面发挥着关键作用，包括缓和欧洲和北大西洋的气温。全球变暖可能导致其崩溃，这被广泛认为是较有可能出现的气候临界点之一。本文利用一个动态空间综合评估模型（S-IAM）考察了此类崩溃的经济影响。模型预测，斯堪的纳维亚和俄罗斯部分地区将遭受显著的GDP与福利损失，而南欧、北非和巴西则因气温略微降低而受益。S-IAM通常预测，全球变暖对低收入地区尤为有害，但AMOC崩溃可能在一定程度上减轻发展中国家部分地区的负面影响，同时却会损害一些较为发达的经济体。这降低了空间不平等，但在中等排放情景下，到2200年全球福利将下降1.9%。NBER工作论文系列的机构订阅者，以及发展中国家的居民，可以在 www.nber.org 免费下载本文。

title: The Economic Geography of Climate Change: Recent Progress and Open Questions
Latent Polarization
On the Measurement of Social Heterogeneity
Climate Change Economics over Time and Space
abstract: With average temperature ranging from −20◦C at the North Pole to 30◦C at the Equator and with global warming expected to reach 1.4◦C to 4.5◦C by the year 2100, it is clear that climate change will have vastly different effects across the globe. Given the abundance of land in northern latitudes, if population and economic activity could freely move across space, the economic cost of global warming would be greatly reduced. But spatial frictions are real: migrants face barriers, trade and transportation are costly, physical infrastructure is not footloose, and knowledge embedded in clusters of economic activity diffuses only imperfectly. Thus, the economic cost of climate change is intimately connected to these spatial frictions. Building on earlier integrated assessment models that largely ignored space, in the past decade there has been significant progress in developing dynamic spatial integrated assessment models (S-IAMs) aimed at providing a more realistic evaluation of the economic cost of climate change, both locally and globally. This review article discusses this progress and provides a guide for future work in this area.
abstract_zh: 从北极的约−20°C到赤道的30°C，平均气温差异巨大，而到2100年全球变暖预计将达到1.4°C至4.5°C，因此显然，气候变化将在全球范围内产生截然不同的影响。鉴于北部纬度地区土地丰富，如果人口和经济活动能够自由地跨越空间迁移，全球变暖的经济成本将大为降低。然而，空间摩擦是真实存在的：移民面临各种障碍，贸易和运输成本高昂，物理基础设施无法随意移动，而蕴含在经济活动集群中的知识只能不完全地扩散。因此，气候变化的经济成本与这些空间摩擦密切相关。在早期大多忽视空间因素的综合评估模型基础上，过去十年间，在发展动态空间综合评估模型（S-IAM）方面已取得显著进展，旨在更加真实地评估气候变化在局部和全球层面的经济成本。本综述文章探讨了这一进展，并为该领域的未来研究提供了指南。

title: Understanding Spatial Variation in COVID-19 across U.S. Counties
Evaluating the Economic Cost of Coastal Flooding
abstract: Sea level rise will cause spatial shifts in economic activity over the next 200 years. Using a spatially disaggregated, dynamic model of the world economy, this paper estimates the consequences of probabilistic projections of local sea level changes. Under an intermediate scenario of greenhouse gas emissions, permanent flooding is projected to reduce global real GDP by 0.19 percent in present value terms. By the year 2200, a projected 1.46 percent of the population will be displaced. Losses in coastal localities are much larger. When ignoring the dynamic response of investment and migration, the loss in real GDP in 2200 increases from 0.11 percent to 4.5 percent. (JEL E23, F01, Q54, Q56)
abstract_zh: 海平面上升将在未来200年内引起经济活动的空间转移。本文利用一个空间细分的世界经济动态模型，估算了局部海平面变化概率预测的后果。在温室气体排放的中等情景下，永久性淹没预计将使全球实际GDP按现值计算减少0.19%。到2200年，预计将有1.46%的人口流离失所。沿海地区的损失要大得多。若忽略投资与移民的动态反应，2200年的实际GDP损失将从0.11%上升至4.5%。（JEL E23, F01, Q54, Q56）
